author: blu
body: The types are data -- they describe what a script does, not how. Emitter functions (PowerShellEmit, BashEmit) pattern-match these types and produce target-shell source text.

author: reek
body: A domain-specific type system for shell script generation. ShellExpr represents values and conditions. ShellCmd represents statements. ShellScript is a complete script with parameters.

author: reek
body: A command's arguments are named, switched or positional. Spelling them as bare text would put the target shell's flag syntax into the caller, which is what this whole type exists to keep out.

author: reek
body: A field of a record literal. The commonest shape a build script still could not say is a TABLE of cases walked by a loop, where some cases carry an extra field the others do not.

author: reek
body: A target that cannot colour drops the attribute and keeps the text.

author: reek
body: A pipeline is a source, a chain of transforms, and a terminal. Counted across the tree the transforms are filter, map, take and sort and nothing else, so the type says those four rather than admitting arbitrary stages; an escape hatch here would rot the way the raw command did.

author: reek
body: SeItem is the element under the cursor. Naming it rather than binding a variable keeps the stage expressions target-independent, since the spelling of the cursor is the emitter's business.

author: reek
body: sp-choices constrains a parameter to a fixed set. An empty list means unconstrained. A shell that refuses a value the script cannot handle refuses it at the boundary, before anything downstream has looked for a file named after it.
